Hey, [USER]. We're actually in the process of adjusting the sleep logic for Streamlit Community Cloud apps _at this very moment_ and you may be noticing one of the changes we're enacting.

The latest logic is: make the app go to sleep after 12h of inactivity.

So maybe your auto-committer is set to an interval longer than 12h? 

Also be aware that we may soon change the definition of "activity" to "user activity" rather than "user activity or commits". And although we don't currently have any plans to block users from programmaticaly keeping their apps up, I can't promise we won't start trying to block them at some point. After all, Streamlit Community Cloud is meant as a free space for the community to share what they're building, and without strong guard rails we'll quickly enter a [tragedy of the commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragedy_of_the_commons) scenario.

If you're using Community Cloud for professional purposes, consider a paid solution, like [Snowflake](https://signup.snowflake.com/?utm_source=streamlit&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=main&utm_content=-ss-github-issue). These can provide much stronger guarantees around uptime, stability, security, and performance.
